newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Bansud share swap gives Banamex more voting clout.
newsitem.headline: Bansud share swap gives Banamex more voting clout.

text.p: A share swap between local shareholders of Argentina's Bansud and Banco Nacional de Mexico SA (Banamex) left unchanged Banamex's controlling stake but gave it more voting power, a top Bansud official said Wednesday.
"The deal means Banamex's voting power rises from 44 percent to 69 percent, more according with its 57 percent stake in Bansud," Bansud Capital Markets manager Marina de Albornoz told Reuters.

Banamex's previous 44 percent voting authority was already enough to take decisions, she added in a telephone interview in reference to the deal announced Tuesday. "It means putting on paper a previous tacit agreement," Albornoz said.

Local shareholders, she said, proved their commitment to the bank by agreeing to restrict the sale of any of their A shares and part of their B shares. That restriction could only be lifted with Banamex's consent.
Bansud had said its local shareholders decided to swap with Banamex part of Bansud's A shares, which carry five votes, for single-vote B shares.
The local shareholders are: Leonardo Anidjar, Oscar Jaratz, Carlos Etcheverrigaray, Carlos Adamo and Ricardo Arriazu.
Shareholders Enrique Jaratz and Rafael Seragopian decided to swap 100 percent of their shares.
Local shareholders also signed an agreement to last until Jan 1, 2002, under which they will remain in charge of Bansud's administration.
"It means a ratification of Banamex's confidence in the Argentine shareholders administering Bansud," Albornoz said.

The agreement also says both Banamex and the local shareholders commit themselves to act jointly through Bansud or its subsidiaries in any financial venture in Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Chile, Paraguay, Peru and Uruguay.
Argentine shareholders have 15.64 percent of Bansud with a 16.94 percent of the voting power. Other shareholders have 27.74 percent of capital and 13.82 percent of votes.
